summary: Configured datauser with a persistent, filesystem-enforced 100 MiB quota scoped to /srv/data. Verified enforcement before and after reboot; persistent data and quota settings recovered successfully.
actions_performed: Created a dedicated 512 MiB XFS filesystem for /srv/data.
Enabled persistent XFS user-quota accounting and enforcement.
Set datauser soft and hard limits to 100 MiB.
Confirmed oversized writes fail with “Disk quota exceeded.”
Restarted node1 safely and verified its boot identity changed.
Verified the mount, quota, account, and checksum-protected data recovered after restart.

evidence.requirement: datauser is limited to 100 MB under /srv/data by the filesystem
evidence.summary: Shows /srv/data mounted as XFS with usrquota, 100M soft and hard limits for datauser, and a 110 MiB write failing with Disk quota exceeded.

evidence.requirement: Configuration and enforcement persist across restart
evidence.summary: After restart, the mount was active with usrquota, accounting and enforcement were ON, limits remained 100M, persistent data retained its checksum, and an oversized write was still rejected.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID ebf808c5-68cd-4bb5-9787-d13d77dbb1c3, acknowledged the scheduled safe reboot, proved the new boot ID 255ff88e-89fa-4cec-a823-7e652ef9d451, and confirmed recovered filesystem, quota, account, and data health.
